purpose: Recast the graphic-AF3 nowhere-zero tension target as one zero-label basis problem in an extremely simple partition matroid: one two-element sign block per graph edge. This imports modern group-labeled-matroid language exactly, while exposing the decisive firewall that the label group has dimension equal to the cycle rank and hence exponential order on the 4-regular hard source.

construction.input: A connected graph G=(V,E), with an arbitrary orientation of E.
construction.cycle_matrix: Choose any full-row-rank signed cycle-basis matrix Q over GF(3). It has beta=|E|-|V|+1 rows and ker(Q)=im(B^T), the GF(3) tension space.
construction.partition_matroid: For every edge e create two ground elements e_plus and e_minus in one rank-one partition block. A basis chooses exactly one token from every edge block.
construction.labels: Let q_e be column e of Q. Label e_plus by q_e and e_minus by -q_e.
construction.sign_decode: A basis X determines s(X) in {+1,-1}^E by s_e=+1 when e_plus is chosen and s_e=-1 when e_minus is chosen.

theorem.name: THREE_COLORING_IFF_ZERO_LABEL_BASE_OF_TWO_CHOICE_PARTITION_MATROID
theorem.statement: G is properly 3-colourable iff the constructed partition matroid has a basis X with psi(X)=0 in Gamma.
proof: Every matroid basis selects exactly one sign token per edge, so s(X) has no zero coordinate.
psi(X)=0 iff Q s(X)=0 iff s(X) belongs to ker(Q), which equals the graphic tension space im(B^T).
Therefore a zero-label basis is exactly a nowhere-zero GF(3) tension.
By the v5.2 tension theorem, nowhere-zero GF(3) tensions are exactly proper 3-colourings modulo one global colour shift per connected component.
For connected G, fix one root colour to zero and reconstruct the unique potential c with B^T c=s(X) by a spanning-tree traversal; this is polynomial.
theorem.counting_control: For connected G, the number of zero-label bases equals P_G(3)/3, because each tension has exactly three globally shifted colour potentials. Counting is only a replay identity, not the algorithmic target.

hard_source_scaling.four_regular: For a connected 4-regular graph on n vertices, |E|=2n and beta=n+1.
hard_source_scaling.group_order: Hence |Gamma|=3^(n+1). The matroid itself has only 4n ground elements and a trivial partition representation, but the exact zero label is a vector in a linearly growing product group.
hard_source_scaling.c4_source: When the complementary 2-factor consists of C4s, their local U_{2,4} structure is already contained in the corresponding cycle rows of Q; the remaining rows are precisely the mixed-cycle compatibility information isolated in v5.3.

results: Horsch-Imolay-Mizutani-Oki-Schwarcz study group-labeled bases/common bases. F-avoiding common bases admit randomized algebraic algorithms for finite groups represented by operation tables, and several fixed-group/fixed-forbidden-set cases are polynomial.
Congruency-constrained matroid-base algorithms are fixed-parameter/polynomial for fixed modulus or fixed finite-group parameters in important cases.
firewall: Those results do not give a polynomial algorithm here by treating Gamma as an explicit finite group: Gamma has order 3^beta=3^(Theta(n)) on the frozen source.
Our target is ZERO label, not merely avoidance of one forbidden label. The zero-basis side is specifically among the difficult cases in the group-labeled-matroid literature.

Replacing Gamma by a polynomial-size hash is not sound without a new source-specific theorem; the earlier full-nonzero-syndrome hash barrier already warns against generic dimension-reducing linear hashes.

positive: All binary sign choices and all mixed cycle equations are unified in one exact matroid-plus-group object with polynomially many ground elements.
Witness reconstruction from any zero-label basis is a linear-time/polynomial spanning-tree integration followed by a direct edge check.
The formulation identifies the only superconstant parameter in generic group-labeled methods: the cycle-rank dimension beta.
killed: Invoke a fixed-finite-group or operation-table group-labeled matroid algorithm and count its group dependence as polynomial in the graph input.
Treat the local U_{2,4} bases as sufficient after discarding the linear-size mixed-label group.
Claim that a polynomial ground-set partition matroid representation alone makes the zero-label basis problem tractable.
not_killed: A graphic-specific compression of the GF(3)^beta zero label that avoids generic hashing and exploits the cycle matrix Q.
An interlacement/transition-matroid contraction that implicitly enforces many mixed cycle coordinates at once.
A deterministic or randomized algebraic zero-test whose complexity is polynomial in beta rather than exponential in |Gamma|, with exact reconstruction/error handling appropriate to the claimed scope.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_ZERO_LABEL_CYCLE_RANK_COMPRESSION_V5_6
next_target.directive: Do not enumerate Gamma or its characters. Work with the explicit beta by 2n graphic cycle matrix Q and one +/- choice per edge. Seek a source-specific polynomial contraction of the vector zero-label condition, preferably using Hamiltonian interlacement/transition structure, that preserves exact existence and reconstructs a sign basis. Any candidate must replay the v5.3 8-vertex mixed-cycle false positive and the NP-hard 4-regular Hamiltonian source.

sources: Florian Horsch, Andras Imolay, Ryuhei Mizutani, Taihei Oki, Tamas Schwarcz, Problems on Group-labeled Matroid Bases, ICALP 2024.
Siyue Liu and Chao Xu, On the Congruency-Constrained Matroid Base, 2023/2024.
